title: One retry owner
lesson: An agent's retry loop can multiply a tool's retries; one code-enforced policy bounds attempts and total waiting.
limitations: Illustrative read-only code search; timing and attempt limits are examples, not production recommendations or recovery guarantees.
The two waits show one sampled jittered-backoff sequence; many-client de-synchronization is not demonstrated.
One six-second downstream budget includes calls and backoff waits; the third attempt’s response wait ends early at that deadline. Client stopping does not cancel already running remote work.
Retry limits and permissions require harness/tool enforcement with SDK retries accounted for; persistent prompts alone do not enforce them.
Audio was analyzed for levels, cue timing and spectrum, not physically listened to; no comparative quality recommendation is claimed.

transcript.text: A code-search request passes from the agent through a read tool to the code index. One service call succeeds and the result returns.
The index becomes unresponsive. The agent invokes the tool twice, and the tool makes three attempts each time. Six service calls accumulate as the waits time out.
The policy changes in the orchestration code: the agent may invoke the tool once, and the tool alone owns up to three total service attempts, including the initial call. A six-second budget appears.
The tool makes three reads with two sampled backoff waits of 1.3 and 1.8 seconds. The same time budget drains during calls and waits. These timings illustrate one scenario, not a guarantee.

The overall budget expires before the last call can use its full individual timeout. The tool stops at three calls and returns a failed tool result; the agent hands off without restarting the read. The index still shows Unresponsive: no result was observed, which does not establish whether remote execution stopped. The result holds, then the screen fades to black.

corrections.scope: transcript and limitation wording only; scene and encoded media unchanged
changes: Distinguished a failed tool result from evidence about the remote outcome; replaced an unsupported unavailable assertion.
Clarified that the third response wait, not a third backoff, is cut short.
